note: Part of many feeling words: 小心 xiǎo xīn, 開心 kāi xīn, 放心 fàng xīn, 擔心 dān xīn, 心情 xīn qíng. The physical organ is 心臟 xīn zàng.
Introduces an extreme case, often with 連 lián…都 dōu: 他甚至連飯都沒吃 tā shèn zhì lián fàn dōu méi chī 'he didn't even eat'.

example.trad: 他很忙，甚至沒時間吃飯。
example.pinyin: Tā hěn máng, shènzhì méi shíjiān chīfàn.
example.english: He's so busy he doesn't even have time to eat.

note: Official documents write it another way, but it sounds the same. 台 tái alone is short for Taiwan: 台北 tái běi, 台語 tái yǔ (Taiwanese Hokkien).
記得 jì de + verb = 'remember to…': 記得帶傘 jì de dài sǎn 'remember to bring an umbrella'. The second syllable is a neutral de (the same character is also dé and děi).

gloss: wait a moment; in a bit; etc.
note: Said alone it means 'Wait!'. In Taiwan it also means 'in a bit, later': 我等等再打給你 wǒ děng děng zài dǎ gěi nǐ. After a list it means 'etc.'.
Often 談一談 tán yī tán or 談談 tán tán 'have a talk' (in tán yī tán the middle yī is said lightly); 談戀愛 tán liàn ài 'to date, be in a relationship'. Casual chatting is 聊 liáo.
Counted with 隻 zhī: 一隻狗 yī zhī gǒu. 狗狗 gǒu gǒu is a cute way to say it.

example.pinyin: Wǒ jiā yǒu yī zhī gǒu.
example.english: We have a dog at home.

note: 每 měi + measure word + noun; 個 gè is the default: 每個人 měi ge rén 'everyone', 每個月 měi ge yuè 'every month'. The second syllable is light (ge), sometimes full gè.

example.pinyin: Měi ge rén dōu hěn xǐhuān tā.

note: Can take an object (改變計畫 gǎi biàn jì huà 'change the plan'). Compare 變 biàn 'to become different'.
Mostly after a verb: 吃完 chī wán 'finish eating', 做完 zuò wán 'finish doing', 用完 yòng wán 'used up'.
Everyday speech more often says 不一樣 bù yī yàng. 不同的 bù tóng de + noun = 'different (kinds of)…'.
連 lián X 都 dōu/也 yě… = 'even X…': 連他都知道 lián tā dōu zhī dào 'even he knows'. As a verb it means 'to connect': 連網路 lián wǎng lù 'connect to the internet'.

example.pinyin: Tā lián yī jù huà dōu méi shuō.
example.english: He didn't even say a word.

note: Formal. In speech, people usually say 這樣 zhè yàng or 這麼 zhè me, but 原來如此 yuán lái rú cǐ 'I see!' is very common.

example.english: I see, now I get it.

gloss: to see; to catch sight of
note: Means the same as 看到 kàn dào, which is more common in everyday speech. MOE gives a neutral second syllable (kàn jian); kàn jiàn is also commonly heard.

example.trad: 你有沒有看見我的手機？
example.pinyin: Nǐ yǒu méiyǒu kànjian wǒ de shǒujī?

note: Adds emphasis, often with mild annoyance: 真是的 zhēn shì de! 'honestly!'. Taiwan keeps the full tone on 是 shì (mainland often zhēn shi).

example.english: It's really way too hot today!

note: Counts flat things: paper, photos, tickets, tables, beds, faces (一張紙 yī zhāng zhǐ). Also a very common surname. The reading zhàng is rare.
Taiwan keeps the full tone on 面 miàn (mainland often lǐ mian). Goes after a noun: 冰箱裡面 bīng xiāng lǐ miàn 'inside the fridge'.

hint: one of a group just mentioned
note: Refers back to a group just mentioned: 其中一個 qí zhōng yī ge 'one of them'.

example.trad: 我有三個孩子，其中一個在美國。
example.pinyin: Wǒ yǒu sān ge háizi, qízhōng yī ge zài Měiguó.
example.english: I have three kids; one of them is in America.

gloss: to fall; to drop; to lose
note: After another verb it means 'away, off': 丟掉 diū diào 'throw away', 忘掉 wàng diào 'forget completely'.
Also used for taking transport: 坐捷運 zuò jié yùn 'take the MRT'. Taiwan also often says 搭 dā for this.

example.pinyin: Nǐ xiān zuò yīxià, wǒ mǎshàng lái.
example.english: Have a seat, I'll be right there.

note: Agrees to a request ('can you help me?' 'no problem!'), or says nothing is wrong: 這樣沒問題 zhè yàng méi wèn tí 'this is fine'. Built from 沒 méi + 問題 wèn tí 'problem'.

example.pinyin: Méi wèntí, jiāo gěi wǒ ba!
example.english: No problem, leave it to me!

note: A more formal version of 讓 ràng, which is far more common in speech. Also seen in 使用 shǐ yòng 'to use'. The reading shì (envoy) is literary.

example.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì shǐ tā hěn nánguò.

note: Usually paired with 但是 dàn shì or 可是 kě shì in the next clause: 雖然很貴 suī rán hěn guì, 但是很好吃 dàn shì hěn hǎo chī 'it's pricey, but tasty'.

example.pinyin: Suīrán hěn lèi, dànshì hěn kāixīn.

note: A very common hedge: 好像是 hǎo xiàng shì 'I think it's…'. Also 'to look just like' in 好像 hǎo xiàng…一樣 yī yàng.
Combines widely: 發訊息 fā xùn xí 'send a message', 發燒 fā shāo 'have a fever', 發脾氣 fā pí qì 'lose one's temper'. Don't confuse it with fǎ 'hair' (頭髮 tóu fǎ), a different word with a third tone.

example.pinyin: Wǒ děng yīxià fā xùnxí gěi nǐ.
example.english: I'll send you a message in a bit.

hint: a way to solve a problem
note: 沒辦法 méi bàn fǎ 'there's no way / it can't be helped' is extremely common.

example.pinyin: Méi bànfǎ, wǒmen zhǐ néng děng.
example.english: Nothing we can do; we just have to wait.

note: Polyphone: the other reading hè means 'to shout', as in 喝采 hè cǎi 'to cheer'; rare in speech.

example.english: What would you like to drink?

note: Common as 好美 hǎo měi 'so beautiful'. Also short for America (美國 měi guó), as in 美金 měi jīn 'US dollars'.

example.english: The view here is so beautiful!

note: Before a verb it means 'hard to…' (難學 nán xué 'hard to learn'), and in some words 'unpleasant to…': 難吃 nán chī 'tastes bad', 難看 nán kàn 'ugly'. Other reading nàn 'disaster', as in 災難 zāi nàn.
Marks an action happening right now: 我正在吃飯 wǒ zhèng zài chī fàn 'I'm eating right now'. Often shortened to just 在 zài.

example.trad: 我正在開車，等一下打給你。
example.pinyin: Wǒ zhèngzài kāichē, děng yīxià dǎ gěi nǐ.
example.english: I'm driving; I'll call you back in a bit.

example.pinyin: Qíshí wǒ bù tài xǐhuān chī là.
example.english: Actually, I don't really like spicy food.

note: 走路 zǒu lù means 'to walk'; 路上 lù shàng 'on the way'. Counted with 條 tiáo.

example.pinyin: Tā shì wǒ zhēnzhèng de péngyǒu.
example.english: He's a true friend of mine.

gloss: to divide; to share; minute; point
note: Also a minute in clock time (三點十分 sān diǎn shí fēn), a point or grade, or a cent. Other reading fèn, as in 部分 bù fèn and 過分 guò fèn 'excessive'.
Also in 馬上 mǎ shàng 'right away' and 馬路 mǎ lù 'road'. Also a common surname.
MOE gives a neutral second syllable (gù shi) for 'story'; gù shì is also commonly heard in Taiwan.

example.trad: 講個故事給我聽好不好？
example.pinyin: Jiǎng ge gùshi gěi wǒ tīng hǎo bù hǎo?
example.english: Will you tell me a story?

note: Taiwan says bù fèn (also written 部份 bù fèn); MOE's headword gives bù fen for this sense, as does mainland speech. 大部分 dà bù fèn 'most'.
Goes right before the verb: 我剛到 wǒ gāng dào 'I just got here'. Means the same as 剛剛 gāng gāng.

example.english: I just got off work, so tired.

note: 餓死了 è sǐ le 'starving' is very common. The opposite is 飽 bǎo 'full'.
For 'live somewhere' use 住 zhù; for 'life, to live (one's life)' use 生活 shēng huó.
Goes after the nouns it relates: 我們之間 wǒ men zhī jiān 'between us', 你跟他之間 nǐ gēn tā zhī jiān 'between you and him'.

example.english: There are no secrets between us.

note: Counted with 本 běn: 一本書 yī běn shū. 讀書 dú shū means 'to study'.

example.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì wǒ lái chǔlǐ.

note: In questions it adds impatience: 你到底要不要 nǐ dào dǐ yào bù yào? 'Do you want it or not?' Also 'to the end', as in 堅持到底 jiān chí dào dǐ 'stick it out to the end'.

example.pinyin: Nǐ dàodǐ yào bù yào qù?
example.english: So are you going or not?

gloss: to contact; to get in touch
note: The usual Taiwan word; the mainland more often says 聯繫 lián xì.

example.pinyin: Dào le zài gēn nǐ liánluò.
example.english: I'll get in touch when I arrive.

note: More formal than 進 jìn or 進去 jìn qù; used for entering a place, a company, a stage.

example.pinyin: Tā jìnrù le yī jiā xīn gōngsī.
